Alex.confusing: The doubling for Meowfia stakes, which the Grudge text described as extra on top of the 2x rule, and how the Owl and Hawk egg rules work. Players at the table argued over whether the Owl's egg goes in its own nest or the target's.
Alex.fun: Round 1, when I pushed the table onto Drew with a fake Hawk claim and a big stake. It paid off with a huge score.
Alex.change: Make the Owl and Hawk egg wording unambiguous, and give a plain-language summary of each night result at dawn so claims are easier to check.
Alex.regret: In round 3 I threw at Blair to split the vote away from my partner Casey, but Casey was already the consensus target. I should have thrown nothing or one low card at the likely loser to avoid looking tied to her. I also slipped in round 1 by saying I visited Blair and then had to patch the claim.

Blair.confusing: The Owl's wording about whose nest receives the egg, which several players argued over in round 1. Round 2's hugged and confused reports were also hard to untangle from the claims.
Blair.fun: Round 3, where Casey's Owl story and Drew's Hawk gain pointed at the same Meowfia, and our Farm side read it correctly and won.
Blair.change: Make the dawn reports say plainly when a visit was hugged or blocked, so players don't have to guess what their own result means.
Blair.regret: In round 1 I threw my stake at Drew based on Casey's Falcon story, and Drew was Farm. I would have held back and questioned Alex's Hawk claim before committing cards.

Casey.confusing: The Owl and Falcon wording was ambiguous in round 1: whether "their nest" meant the target's or the Owl's. It also wasn't clear how the huge final bonus scores were calculated.
Casey.fun: Round 2, as the Floofer, when Finley and Blair both said they were hugged after visiting me and I bluffed an Owl claim to deflect. Setting Alex and Drew against each other was a good moment.
Casey.change: Show the exact scoring formula and the bonus breakdown during play, so decisions about stakes are easier to weigh.
Casey.regret: In round 3 I winked Drew, a verified Hawk whose accusation of me was true. That made me look guilty, and I also confirmed his role aloud. I should have kept the Wink, claimed Owl more carefully, and thrown at a Farm player who wasn't a confirmed claim.

Drew.confusing: The Hawk's egg gain is ambiguous when a Turkey is in play, because a Turkey also gives an egg to each visitor. I took my +1 from visiting Alex as proof Alex was Meowfia, but Alex was the Turkey.
Drew.fun: Round 3's day, where Casey's Owl report and my Hawk claim collided and Ellis and Finley turned the table against her, and the eggsecution flipped it to a Farm win.
Drew.change: Make it clearer which animals give eggs to their visitors and which only gain on a specific condition, so a +1 can be read without guessing at Turkeys.
Drew.regret: In round 2 I treated my Hawk +1 on Alex as proof Alex was Meowfia and pushed the table to throw at him, when Alex was the Turkey who pays visitors. I should have checked whether any other animal could explain the egg before calling it.

Ellis.confusing: The Owl's wording ("lay an egg in their nest") was ambiguous, and players argued over whose nest it meant. The Grudge doubling in the round 1 resolution text also wasn't in the rules I was given.
Ellis.fun: Round 3, when Casey confirmed Drew was the Hawk and I could argue that his +1 proved Casey was Meowfia. The table then converged on her and Farm won.
Ellis.change: Show each player's role-specific rule text, including the Owl's, at the start of every round. That would cut the table arguments over wording.
Ellis.regret: In round 2 I claimed Falcon and made up a visit that contradicted Finley's story, and that drew a throw at me. I should have given a vaguer claim, or used my Mouser info on someone more useful than Blair.

Finley.confusing: Owl and Turkey egg rules were easy to misread, and the Tit's "lay an egg if they are that role" meant my Pigeon guess gave me an egg from a Turkey, not a Pigeon. I wrongly announced Blair as a Pigeon.
Finley.fun: Round 3, when Ellis's Eagle claim was verified by my Kookaburra visit and the table converged on Casey, the Owl and Hawk egg counts forced a real contradiction to surface.
Finley.change: Make the nest-change and egg-source information clearer at dawn, so players can tell which animal caused each egg gain without having to infer it from other players' claims.
Finley.regret: In Round 1 I publicly called Blair a Pigeon based on an egg I gained from a Turkey visit, which was a false claim. I would instead say only that my visit gained an egg and that it fit a Turkey, and I'd avoid naming a role I hadn't verified.
